# RFC-0001: aoska-facing omactl CLI and JSON contract

> **Version:** 0.1.0 | **Status:** draft | **Phase:** spec

---

## 1. Summary

### [RFC-0001:C-SUMMARY] Summary (Informative) <a id="rfc-0001c-summary"></a>

This RFC specifies the omactl command-line contract consumed by aoska for package-management queries, planning, operation execution, and unit inspection.

**Scope:** This RFC covers the aoska-facing `omactl capabilities`, `omactl query`, `omactl plan`, `omactl run`, `omactl status`, `omactl result`, and `omactl logs` surfaces; required command arguments; JSON envelope and payload fields; error codes; exit status; unit identifiers; log streaming; and argument-safety requirements.

**Out of scope:** This RFC does not specify aoska UI behavior, aoska static catalog metadata, oma's internal Rust APIs, or omactl implementation structure beyond the externally observable CLI contract.

**Rationale:** aoska needs a stable GUI-safe integration surface. omactl should mediate process, systemd, and JSON transport concerns while delegating package-management semantics to oma.

---

## 2. Specification

### [RFC-0001:C-OWNERSHIP] Ownership Boundaries (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-ownership"></a>

oma MUST own package-management semantics, including dependency resolution, operation planning, TUM matching, security-update classification, and package metadata derived from APT state.

omactl MUST own process mediation, systemd transient unit creation, unit naming, unit status retrieval, unit logs, unit results, and the aoska-facing JSON envelope.

omactl MUST NOT reimplement dependency resolution or package-management semantics that belong to oma.

omactl MAY delegate query, planning, and operation semantics to the system-installed oma binary or to an explicitly configured oma binary path.

**Rationale:** The API boundary keeps omactl small and lets aoska depend on one process-level contract instead of embedding package-manager crates.

### [RFC-0001:C-COMMAND-SURFACE] Command Surface (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-command-surface"></a>

omactl MUST expose aoska-facing package-management capabilities through `capabilities`, `query`, `plan`, `run`, `status`, `result`, `logs`, and `cancel` command groups.

`omactl capabilities --json` MUST return the supported aoska-facing capability identifiers.

`omactl query <topic> --json [args...]` MUST be reserved for read-only package state retrieval.

`omactl plan <operation> --json [args...]` MUST be reserved for read-only computation of package operations that would be performed.

`omactl run <operation> --json [args...]` MUST be reserved for scheduling package-management operations that may change package state, package metadata state, or other oma-managed operation state.

Refresh and check-update operations scheduled through `omactl run refresh` MUST be treated as long-running package-management operations even when they do not install, remove, or upgrade packages.

`omactl status --json <unit>` MUST return machine-readable status for a unit started by omactl.

`omactl result --json <unit>` MUST return machine-readable terminal or current result information for a unit started by omactl.

`omactl logs --json <unit>` MUST return machine-readable accumulated logs for a unit started by omactl.

`omactl logs --json --follow <unit>` MUST stream log events as JSON Lines.

`omactl cancel --json <unit>` MUST request cancellation for a unit started by omactl.

**Rationale:** Distinct command groups make intent testable and let aoska call the correct class of operation without knowing oma internals.

### [RFC-0001:C-JSON-ENVELOPE] JSON Envelope (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-json-envelope"></a>

All aoska-facing successful outputs MUST be available as a single JSON document unless the command explicitly documents JSON Lines.

All aoska-facing JSON documents MUST include `schema_version`, `ok`, and `kind` fields.

`schema_version` MUST be the integer `1` for this version of the contract.

Successful JSON documents MUST set `ok` to `true` and place command-specific payload under `data` unless the command documents a more specific payload location.

Failed JSON documents MUST set `ok` to `false` and include an `error` object.

The `error` object MUST include `code` as a stable ASCII string.

The `error` object MUST include `message` as a human-readable string.

The `error` object MAY include `details` as an object.

Machine-readable field names, error codes, and enum-like values MUST be stable ASCII strings.

JSON output MUST NOT contain terminal color escape sequences.

JSON output MUST NOT use localized field names.

Producers MAY add fields within a schema version.

Producers MUST NOT remove fields within a schema version.

Producers MUST NOT rename fields within a schema version.

Producers MUST NOT change field semantics within a schema version.

Consumers MUST ignore unknown fields.

Breaking JSON changes MUST increment `schema_version`.

**Rationale:** aoska needs one parse path across omactl and oma-backed operations, and independently released components need forward-compatible JSON.

### [RFC-0001:C-QUERY] Read-only Query Operations (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-query"></a>

`omactl query` MUST NOT modify package state.

`omactl query` MUST reject requested actions that are not read-only.

`omactl query upgradable --json` MUST return kind `omactl.query.upgradable`.

`omactl query upgradable --json` MUST return `data.packages` as an array.

Each upgradable package object MUST include `name`, `architecture`, `current_version`, and `new_version` as strings.

Each upgradable package object MUST include `held` as a boolean when held-package state is available.

`omactl query package-detail --json <package>...` MUST return kind `omactl.query.package-detail`.

`omactl query package-detail --json <package>...` MUST reject an empty package list with error code `INVALID_ARGUMENTS`.

`omactl query package-detail --json <package>...` MUST return `data.packages` as an array.

Each package detail object MUST include `name` as a string.

Each package detail object SHOULD include `version`, `architecture`, `summary`, and `description` as strings when those values are available from oma.

Each package detail object SHOULD include `installed` and `upgradable` as booleans when those values are available from oma.

`omactl query search --json <term>...` MAY return kind `omactl.query.search` when `query.search.v1` is advertised.

`omactl query search --json <term>...` MUST reject an empty search term list with error code `INVALID_ARGUMENTS` when search is supported.

`omactl query search --json <term>...` MUST return `data.results` as an array when search is supported.

Each search result object MUST include `name` as a string.

Each search result object SHOULD include `version`, `architecture`, and `summary` as strings when those values are available from oma.

Each search result object SHOULD include `installed` and `exact_match` as booleans when those values are available from oma.

`omactl query` SHOULD execute without creating a systemd transient unit unless system policy requires a mediated execution context.

**Rationale:** aoska renders package and update state frequently, so read paths must be safe, cheap, explicit, and schema-testable.

### [RFC-0001:C-QUERY-INSTALLED] Installed Package Query (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-query-installed"></a>

`omactl query installed --json` MUST NOT modify package state.

`omactl query installed --json` MUST return kind `omactl.query.installed`.

`omactl query installed --json` MUST return `data.packages` as an array.

Each installed package object MUST include `name` as a string.

Each installed package object MUST include `architecture` as a string.

Each installed package object MUST include `current_version` as a string.

Each installed package object MAY include `new_version` as a string when an upgrade candidate is available.

Each installed package object MUST include `branches` as an array of strings.

Each installed package object MUST include `status` as a stable ASCII string.

Each installed package object MUST include `installed` as a boolean.

Each installed package object MUST include `upgradable` as a boolean.

Each installed package object MUST include `held` as a boolean.

Each installed package object MUST include `automatic` as a boolean.

For `omactl query installed --json`, package objects representing installed packages MUST set `installed` to `true`.

`upgradable` MUST be `true` when `new_version` is present for that package.

`upgradable` MUST be `false` when omactl can determine that no upgrade candidate exists for that package.

When a delegated oma JSON field is unavailable, omactl MUST either derive the field from another machine-readable oma JSON field or withhold `query.installed.v1` from capability discovery.

**Rationale:** aoska needs an installed inventory for update and uninstall views with stable booleans instead of display text scraped from package-manager output.


### [RFC-0001:C-PLAN] Planning Operations (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-plan"></a>

`omactl plan` MUST NOT modify package state.

`omactl plan upgrade --json [package]...` MUST return kind `omactl.plan.upgrade`.

`omactl plan install --json <package>...` MUST return kind `omactl.plan.install`.

`omactl plan install --json <package>...` MUST reject an empty package list with error code `INVALID_ARGUMENTS`.

`omactl plan remove --json <package>...` MUST return kind `omactl.plan.remove`.

`omactl plan remove --json <package>...` MUST reject an empty package list with error code `INVALID_ARGUMENTS`.

Planning output MUST include `data.operation.install` as an array.

Planning output MUST include `data.operation.remove` as an array.

Planning output MUST include `data.operation.total_download_size` as an integer number of bytes.

Planning output MUST include `data.operation.disk_size_delta` as an integer number of bytes.

Planning output MUST include `data.operation.recommend` as an array when recommended packages are reported by oma.

Planning output MUST include `data.operation.suggest` as an array when suggested packages are reported by oma.

Each install entry MUST include `name`, `architecture`, and `new_version` as strings.

Each install entry SHOULD include `old_version`, `download_size`, and `operation` when those values are reported by oma.

Each remove entry MUST include `name` and `architecture` as strings.

Each remove entry SHOULD include `version` and `reason` when those values are reported by oma.

Planning output MUST include `data.held_packages` as an array when held-package information is available.

When `plan.tum.v1` is advertised, planning output MUST include `data.tum.available` as a boolean.

When `data.tum.available` is `true`, planning output MUST include `data.tum.matches` as an array.

Each TUM match MUST include `manifest_name` as a string.

Each TUM match MUST include `is_security` as a boolean.

Each TUM match MUST include `package_names` as an array of strings.

Each TUM match SHOULD include `name` and `caution` localized maps when those values are available.

Localized TUM maps MUST be JSON objects whose keys are locale identifiers and whose values are strings.

When TUM data is unavailable, planning output MUST set `data.tum.available` to `false` and SHOULD include `data.tum.reason` as a stable ASCII string.

**Rationale:** aoska needs operation previews and security-update grouping without linking to oma crates or reimplementing planning logic.

### [RFC-0001:C-SELECTED-UPGRADE] Selected Upgrade Semantics (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-selected-upgrade"></a>

`omactl plan upgrade --json [package]...` MUST treat an empty package list as a request to plan all available upgrades.

`omactl plan upgrade --json [package]...` MUST treat a non-empty package list as a request to plan upgrades for only the selected package names.

`omactl plan upgrade --json <package>...` MUST return kind `omactl.plan.upgrade` when selected-upgrade planning is supported.

Selected-upgrade planning output for a non-empty package list MUST include `data.selection` as an object.

Selected-upgrade planning output for a non-empty package list MUST include `data.selection.requested` as an array containing the requested package names in request order.

Selected-upgrade planning output for a non-empty package list MUST include `data.selection.not_upgradable` as an array containing requested package names that are known to exist but cannot be upgraded.

Selected-upgrade planning output for a non-empty package list MUST include `data.selection.not_found` as an array containing requested package names that are not found in available package metadata.

Selected-upgrade planning MUST return a successful JSON response and exit status `0` when omactl can produce a valid plan, even when `data.selection.not_upgradable` or `data.selection.not_found` is non-empty.

Selected-upgrade planning MUST return a failed JSON response and a non-zero exit status when omactl cannot determine the selected-upgrade plan or required selection fields from machine-readable oma output.

Selected-upgrade planning output MUST NOT silently plan unrelated package upgrades except dependencies, removals, or related operations required by the package manager to complete the selected upgrade.

`omactl run upgrade --json [--unit <unit>] [--yes] [package]...` MUST treat an empty package list as a request to schedule all available upgrades.

`omactl run upgrade --json [--unit <unit>] [--yes] [package]...` MUST treat a non-empty package list as a request to schedule upgrades for only the selected package names.

Selected-upgrade execution MUST pass selected package names to oma as argv elements.

Selected-upgrade execution MUST NOT build shell command strings from selected package names.

Scheduling success for selected-upgrade execution MUST return kind `omactl.operation.started`.

Scheduling success for selected-upgrade execution MUST include `data.operation` as `upgrade`.

Scheduling success for selected-upgrade execution for a non-empty package list MUST include `data.selection` as an object.

Scheduling success for selected-upgrade execution for a non-empty package list MUST include `data.selection.requested` as an array containing the requested package names in request order.

Scheduling success for selected-upgrade execution for a non-empty package list MUST include `data.selection.not_upgradable` as an array when omactl performed pre-scheduling selection validation; otherwise it MUST be an empty array.

Scheduling success for selected-upgrade execution for a non-empty package list MUST include `data.selection.not_found` as an array when omactl performed pre-scheduling selection validation; otherwise it MUST be an empty array.

Selected-upgrade execution MUST reject the request with error code `INVALID_ARGUMENTS`, a non-zero exit status, and `error.details.selection` containing `requested`, `not_upgradable`, and `not_found` arrays when pre-scheduling validation determines that every requested package is either not found or not upgradable.

omactl MUST NOT advertise `plan.upgrade.selected.v1` unless selected-upgrade planning satisfies this clause.

omactl MUST NOT advertise `run.upgrade.selected.v1` unless selected-upgrade execution satisfies this clause.

**Rationale:** aoska needs both "update all" and user-selected update flows, and scripts must be able to distinguish all-upgrade requests from selected-upgrade requests without relying on ambiguous option ordering.

### [RFC-0001:C-RUN] Operation Execution (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-run"></a>

`omactl run upgrade --json [--unit <unit>] [--yes] [package]...` MUST schedule an upgrade operation through a systemd transient unit.

`omactl run install --json [--unit <unit>] [--yes] <package>...` MUST schedule an install operation through a systemd transient unit.

`omactl run install --json` MUST reject an empty package list with error code `INVALID_ARGUMENTS`.

`omactl run remove --json [--unit <unit>] [--yes] <package>...` MUST schedule a remove operation through a systemd transient unit.

`omactl run remove --json` MUST reject an empty package list with error code `INVALID_ARGUMENTS`.

`omactl run` MUST execute the system-installed oma binary or an explicitly configured oma binary path.

`omactl run` MUST pass package names, paths, and flags to oma as argv elements.

`omactl run` MUST NOT build shell command strings from caller-provided package names, paths, or flags.

`omactl run` MUST reject a caller-provided unit name that collides with an existing systemd unit or an omactl-retained unit with error code `INVALID_ARGUMENTS`.

`omactl run` MUST return kind `omactl.operation.started` on scheduling success.

Scheduling success output MUST include `data.unit` as the scheduled systemd unit name.

Scheduling success output MUST include `data.operation` as one of `upgrade`, `install`, `remove`, or `refresh`.

`omactl run` MUST return scheduling failure synchronously when no unit is scheduled.

`omactl run` MUST reject a package-management operation with error code `OMA_BUSY` when `/run/lock/oma.lock` exists or when omactl can otherwise determine that an oma package-management operation is active.

`omactl run` MAY support concurrent package-management operations only after advertising a future capability that explicitly permits concurrency.

**Rationale:** Package-management operations need privilege, lifetime, cancellation, and logging boundaries that belong outside the GUI process.

### [RFC-0001:C-REFRESH] Refresh and Check-Update Operations (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-refresh"></a>

`omactl run refresh --json --purpose <refresh|check-updates> [--unit <unit>]` MUST schedule a metadata refresh or check-update operation through a systemd transient unit.

`omactl run refresh --json` MUST reject a missing or invalid `--purpose` value with error code `INVALID_ARGUMENTS`.

The `refresh` purpose MUST mean refreshing package metadata for general package-management use.

The `check-updates` purpose MUST mean refreshing or validating package metadata specifically before checking for available updates.

`omactl run refresh --json --purpose <refresh|check-updates> [--unit <unit>]` MUST return kind `omactl.operation.started` on scheduling success.

Refresh scheduling success output MUST include `data.unit` as the scheduled systemd unit name.

Refresh scheduling success output MUST include `data.operation` as `refresh`.

Refresh scheduling success output MUST include `data.purpose` as either `refresh` or `check-updates`, matching the requested purpose.

Refresh operations MUST use the status, result, and logs inspection surfaces defined for omactl-owned units.

`omactl status --json <refresh-unit>` MUST report refresh progress as `pending`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`, or `unknown` using the same state vocabulary as other omactl-owned units.

`omactl result --json <refresh-unit>` MUST report terminal refresh success, failure, or cancellation using the same state vocabulary as other omactl-owned units.

`omactl logs --json <refresh-unit>` and `omactl logs --json --follow <refresh-unit>` MUST expose refresh logs through the same log payloads as other omactl-owned units.

`omactl cancel --json <refresh-unit>` MUST be supported when `run.refresh.v1` and `unit.cancel.v1` are both advertised and the refresh unit is still cancellable.

omactl MUST return scheduling failure synchronously when no refresh unit is scheduled.

omactl MUST reject a refresh operation with error code `OMA_BUSY` when `/run/lock/oma.lock` exists or when omactl can otherwise determine that an oma package-management operation is active.

**Rationale:** aoska needs a cancellable checking state that is observable through the same operation lifecycle as installs, removals, and upgrades.

### [RFC-0001:C-UNIT-INSPECTION] Unit Inspection (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-unit-inspection"></a>

omactl MUST provide machine-readable status for units it starts.

omactl MUST provide machine-readable result information for units it starts.

omactl MUST provide log retrieval for units it starts.

`omactl status --json <unit>` MUST return kind `omactl.unit.status` for an inspectable unit started by omactl.

`omactl result --json <unit>` MUST return kind `omactl.unit.result` for an inspectable unit started by omactl.

`omactl logs --json <unit>` MUST return kind `omactl.unit.logs` for an inspectable unit started by omactl.

`omactl logs --json --follow <unit>` MUST stream JSON Lines where each line is a JSON envelope.

Each successful follow-mode log event MUST use kind `omactl.unit.log-line`.

Unit status and result payloads MUST include `data.unit` as the unit name.

Unit status and result payloads MUST include `data.state` as one of `pending`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`, or `unknown`.

Unit status and result payloads SHOULD include `data.systemd.ActiveState`, `data.systemd.SubState`, `data.systemd.Result`, and `data.systemd.ExecMainStatus` when those values are available from systemd.

Accumulated log payloads MUST include `data.unit` as the unit name.

Accumulated log payloads MUST include `data.lines` as an array of strings.

Each follow-mode log-line payload MUST include `data.unit` as the unit name.

Each follow-mode log-line payload MUST include `data.line` as a string.

`omactl logs --json --follow <unit>` MUST close stdout and exit with status `0` after the unit reaches a terminal state and available log output has been emitted.

If follow-mode log setup fails before streaming begins, omactl MUST emit one JSON error envelope and exit with a non-zero status.

If follow-mode log streaming fails after one or more log-line envelopes have been emitted, omactl MUST emit a final JSON error envelope with kind `omactl.unit.log-error` when stdout remains writable and exit with a non-zero status.

omactl MUST return error code `UNKNOWN_UNIT` when the requested unit was not started by omactl.

omactl MUST return error code `UNKNOWN_UNIT` for non-omactl systemd units even when systemd could otherwise inspect those units.

**Rationale:** aoska needs deterministic operation state transitions without parsing human-oriented `systemctl` or `journalctl` output, and omactl should not become a generic systemd inspection API by accident.

### [RFC-0001:C-CANCEL] Operation Cancellation (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-cancel"></a>

`omactl cancel --json <unit>` MUST request cancellation for an omactl-owned unit.

`omactl cancel --json <unit>` MUST return kind `omactl.unit.cancel` when the cancellation request is accepted or when the unit is already terminal.

Cancellation output MUST include `data.unit` as the unit name.

Cancellation output MUST include `data.state` as one of `cancelling`, `cancelled`, or `already_terminal`.

Cancellation output SHOULD include `data.previous_state` when omactl knew the unit state before requesting cancellation.

omactl MUST return error code `UNKNOWN_UNIT` when the requested unit was not started by omactl.

omactl MUST return error code `UNKNOWN_UNIT` for non-omactl systemd units even when systemd could otherwise stop those units.

omactl MUST return error code `SYSTEMD_FAILED` when systemd rejects a stop request for an omactl-owned non-terminal unit.

After a cancellation request is accepted, later `status --json` and `result --json` calls MUST map systemd states that indicate a caller-requested stop to `data.state = "cancelled"` when omactl can distinguish the cancellation from ordinary failure.

If omactl cannot distinguish a caller-requested stop from an ordinary failure, `result --json` MUST preserve the raw systemd fields that caused the ambiguity under `data.systemd`.

A terminal state of `cancelled` MUST be used for a unit stopped by `omactl cancel --json <unit>`.

A terminal state of `failed` MUST be used for a unit that completed with a non-zero operation failure and was not known to be caller-cancelled.

A terminal state of `succeeded` MUST be used for a unit that completed successfully.

A terminal state of `unknown` MUST be used only when omactl cannot map the retained unit state to `pending`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, or `cancelled`.

**Rationale:** aoska needs cancel buttons that can target only operations it owns and needs terminal states that distinguish user cancellation from package-manager failure.


### [RFC-0001:C-STORAGE] Optional Storage Summary (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-storage"></a>

`omactl query storage --json` MAY be implemented as a P2 optional capability.

`omactl query storage --json` MUST return kind `omactl.query.storage` when `query.storage.v1` is advertised.

`omactl query storage --json` MUST NOT modify package state.

Storage output MUST include `data.estimated` as a boolean.

Storage output MUST include at least one concrete storage section: `data.filesystems` as a non-empty array, `data.packages` as a non-empty array, or both.

Storage output MUST NOT consist only of `data.estimated` without a concrete storage section.

Storage output MUST set `data.estimated` to `true` when any reported size is approximate, partially available, derived from package metadata that may be stale, or not measured from the filesystem at the time of the query.

Storage output MUST set `data.estimated` to `false` only when all reported sizes are measured or otherwise exact for the query time.

Storage output MAY include `data.filesystems` as an array when filesystem capacity information is available.

Each filesystem entry SHOULD include `mount`, `total_bytes`, `used_bytes`, and `available_bytes` when those values are available.

Storage output MAY include `data.packages` as an array when installed package size information is available.

Each package storage entry SHOULD include `name`, `architecture`, `installed_size_bytes`, and `estimated` when those values are available.

omactl MUST NOT advertise `query.storage.v1` unless it can produce the JSON envelope, estimate markers, and at least one concrete storage section required by this clause.

**Rationale:** Storage summaries are useful for aoska but are not required for the initial package-management migration; explicit estimate markers prevent UI from presenting approximate package sizes as exact accounting.

### [RFC-0001:C-DELEGATED-OMA-JSON] Delegated oma JSON Requirements (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-delegated-oma-json"></a>

omactl MAY wrap machine-readable `oma list --json` output for `query upgradable` and `query installed`.

omactl MAY wrap machine-readable `oma show --json` output for `query package-detail`.

omactl MAY wrap machine-readable `oma search --json` output for `query search`.

When delegated oma JSON is JSON Lines, omactl MUST parse each JSON line as machine-readable data and normalize successful output into the envelope required by this RFC.

When delegated oma JSON is a single JSON document, omactl MUST parse that document as machine-readable data and normalize successful output into the envelope required by this RFC.

omactl MUST validate delegated oma JSON enough to decide whether required omactl payload fields can be produced.

omactl MUST return error code `MALFORMED_DELEGATE_OUTPUT` when delegated oma JSON is malformed or lacks data required for an advertised capability.

omactl MUST NOT parse human-oriented oma dry-run output to satisfy `plan.*` capabilities.

omactl MUST NOT parse human-oriented oma operation output to satisfy `run.*` scheduling or result payload requirements.

omactl MUST NOT parse localized, colored, table-formatted, or progress-oriented oma output as a substitute for delegated JSON.

omactl MAY leave plan, TUM, selected-upgrade, search, storage, or other optional capabilities unadvertised until machine-readable delegated JSON or native omactl data sources satisfy this RFC.

omactl MUST report unsupported delegated oma capabilities as `UNSUPPORTED_COMMAND` or `OMA_EXEC_FAILED` rather than emitting partial success payloads.

**Rationale:** The integration boundary is stable only if omactl consumes machine-readable data from oma and refuses to convert terminal presentation text into an API.


### [RFC-0001:C-ERRORS] Errors and Exit Status (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-errors"></a>

Machine-readable errors MUST include a stable error code.

Machine-readable errors MUST include a human-readable message.

omactl MUST use error code `INVALID_ARGUMENTS` for syntactically invalid commands, missing required arguments, empty package lists where a package list is required, invalid unit names, caller-provided unit-name collisions, or selected-upgrade requests that are rejected before scheduling because no requested package can be upgraded.

omactl MUST use error code `UNSUPPORTED_COMMAND` for valid omactl syntax that requests an unsupported aoska-facing capability.

omactl MUST use error code `OMA_BUSY` when a package-management operation is rejected because another oma package-management operation is active.

omactl MUST use error code `AUTHORIZATION_FAILED` when permission or privilege acquisition fails.

omactl MUST use error code `SYSTEMD_FAILED` when systemd cannot schedule, inspect, stop, or report a required omactl-owned unit.

omactl MUST use error code `OMA_EXEC_FAILED` when the delegated oma command cannot be executed or exits in a way that prevents omactl from producing the required success payload.

omactl MUST use error code `TUM_UNAVAILABLE` when TUM data is required for a requested capability but cannot be obtained.

omactl MUST use error code `UNKNOWN_UNIT` when a requested unit was not started by omactl or is no longer retained by omactl.

omactl MUST use error code `MALFORMED_DELEGATE_OUTPUT` when delegated oma JSON is required but cannot be parsed or validated.

omactl MUST use error code `INTERNAL_ERROR` for unexpected failures not covered by a more specific code.

Error details for `OMA_BUSY` SHOULD include `unit` when the active unit is known.

Error details for `SYSTEMD_FAILED` SHOULD include `unit` and `systemd_message` when available.

Error details for `OMA_EXEC_FAILED` SHOULD include `exit_status` when available.

Error details for `INVALID_ARGUMENTS` SHOULD include `argument` when one argument caused the failure.

Error details for selected-upgrade `INVALID_ARGUMENTS` failures MUST include `selection` when the failure is caused by all requested packages being known before scheduling as not found or not upgradable.

Read-only query and planning commands MUST exit with status `0` only when the JSON response represents a successful query or plan.

Read-only query and planning commands MUST exit with a non-zero status when they cannot produce a successful JSON response.

Operation-start commands MUST exit with status `0` when the operation was successfully scheduled.

Operation-start commands MUST exit with a non-zero status when the operation was not scheduled.

If an operation-start command supports wait mode, wait-mode output MUST distinguish scheduling failure from unit execution failure.

**Rationale:** aoska needs error handling that can drive UI state and diagnostics without guessing from text output.

### [RFC-0001:C-COMPATIBILITY] Compatibility (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-compatibility"></a>

Existing human-oriented omactl commands that do not pass `--json` SHOULD remain compatible for terminal users.

New machine-readable output MUST be exposed through explicit `--json` flags or explicit aoska-facing subcommands.

Existing oma `--json` output MAY be reused behind omactl if omactl wraps or validates it to satisfy this RFC.

omactl MUST document the minimum oma capability required for each aoska-facing command that delegates to oma.

omactl MUST report unsupported delegated oma capabilities as `UNSUPPORTED_COMMAND` or `OMA_EXEC_FAILED` rather than emitting partial success payloads.

**Rationale:** The GUI contract should not break existing command-line workflows, and aoska needs clear version diagnostics.

### [RFC-0001:C-SECURITY] Security and Argument Handling (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-security"></a>

omactl MUST invoke oma without shell interpolation for caller-provided arguments.

omactl MUST validate that `query` and `plan` requests are read-only.

Caller-provided unit names MUST be accepted only when they match `^[A-Za-z0-9_.@-]{1,80}$`.

omactl MUST reject invalid caller-provided unit names with error code `INVALID_ARGUMENTS`.

omactl MUST NOT normalize an invalid caller-provided unit name into a different valid name.

omactl MUST reject caller-provided unit names that collide with an existing systemd unit or an omactl-retained unit.

omactl MUST use error code `INVALID_ARGUMENTS` for caller-provided unit-name collisions.

omactl MUST treat package names and paths as structured argv values, not as shell fragments.

**Rationale:** aoska passes user-influenced package identifiers and operation identifiers to omactl, so the process boundary must not become a command-injection surface or a generic systemd control surface.

### [RFC-0001:C-CAPABILITIES] Capability Discovery (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-capabilities"></a>

`omactl capabilities --json` MUST return a JSON envelope with kind `omactl.capabilities`.

The `data` object for `omactl.capabilities` MUST include `omactl_version` as a string.

The `data` object for `omactl.capabilities` MUST include `oma_path` as a string when an oma binary can be resolved.

The `data` object for `omactl.capabilities` MUST include `oma_version` as a string when the resolved oma binary can report a version.

The `data` object for `omactl.capabilities` MUST include `capabilities` as an array of stable ASCII strings.

The initial aoska-facing capability identifiers MUST include `query.upgradable.v1`, `query.installed.v1`, `query.package-detail.v1`, `plan.upgrade.v1`, `plan.install.v1`, `plan.remove.v1`, `run.upgrade.v1`, `run.install.v1`, `run.remove.v1`, `run.refresh.v1`, `unit.status.v1`, `unit.result.v1`, `unit.logs.v1`, and `unit.cancel.v1` when the corresponding command is supported.

The capability identifier `query.search.v1` MAY be advertised when live package search is supported.

The capability identifier `query.storage.v1` MAY be advertised when optional storage summary output is supported.

The capability identifier `plan.tum.v1` MUST be advertised when planning output can include TUM matching and security-update classification.

The capability identifier `plan.upgrade.selected.v1` MUST be advertised when `omactl plan upgrade --json <package>...` supports a non-empty package list for selected-upgrade planning.

The capability identifier `run.upgrade.selected.v1` MUST be advertised when `omactl run upgrade --json <package>...` supports a non-empty package list for selected-upgrade execution.

omactl MUST NOT advertise a capability identifier unless the command and payload requirements for that capability are satisfied.

omactl MUST NOT advertise `plan.tum.v1`, `plan.upgrade.v1`, `plan.upgrade.selected.v1`, `run.upgrade.selected.v1`, or any other plan capability merely because a human-oriented dry-run or operation command exists.

**Rationale:** Capability discovery gives aoska a programmatic compatibility gate without hard-coding omactl or oma version numbers.
